item: the Host guard and the Origin check no longer serve the test client's name (testserver); the suite lists it through OO_ALLOWED_HOSTS (audit 0.5.0)
summary: The Host-header guard answered 421 to every name but the loopback ones and the operator's OO_ALLOWED_HOSTS, except Starlette's TestClient name, testserver, which was served in the shipped app on the reasoning that the client never opens a socket. testserver is a single-label name nobody owns, and a name resolution that is not DNS (LLMNR, NetBIOS) is answered by whoever answers first on a LAN: a same-LAN attacker could answer it, lure the user to http://testserver:8000 and rebind it to 127.0.0.1, and the page would be same-origin with the API and pass the Host guard (the CSRF middleware already refused it as an Origin). Read from the code, not reproduced. It is now served by nobody by default: one _allowed_hosts() (the loopback names and OO_ALLOWED_HOSTS) feeds both checks, tests/conftest.py appends testserver to OO_ALLOWED_HOSTS for the suite (an operator's own value in the shell is kept), and the two in-process operator tools (the scale bench's endpoint phase and scripts/perf_harness.py) build their TestClient on http://127.0.0.1. Pinned: without the variable testserver is refused as a Host (421, with or without a port, in any case) and as a state-changing request's Host or Origin (403), the loopback names are still served, and with the variable set it is served like any listed name. Not browser-verified. The 515 test files that touch the API were run against the new default (10,843 passed); 15 tests failed there and two modules did not import (scipy and vaderSentiment are not installed in the sandbox, and one file depends on the order of the files before it); every one fails the same way on the commit before this change.
